# Delta Browser

> A Model Context Protocol (MCP) server that gives an AI agent a real web browser
> to drive. 62 tools, Chrome/Edge/Chromium or a managed sandboxed engine, and a
> one-command install. No API keys, no hosted service, no per-run billing.
>
> Canonical repository: https://github.com/DevAnimecx/deltabrowser
> License: Business Source License 1.1 (converts to Apache-2.0 on 2030-01-01).

Delta Browser is for when an AI agent needs to actually open a page: navigating,
clicking, typing, reading rendered text, taking screenshots, and asserting on
results. It is not a hosted browser-automation API. It is a single binary that
sits between an MCP-capable agent and a real browser.

## Install

```sh
# Linux, macOS, WSL
curl -fsSL https://raw.githubusercontent.com/DevAnimecx/deltabrowser/main/scripts/install.sh | sh
```

```powershell
# Windows PowerShell 5.1 or 7
irm https://raw.githubusercontent.com/DevAnimecx/deltabrowser/main/scripts/install.ps1 | iex; Install-DeltaBrowser
```

Verify with `delta doctor`. It reports the engine, sandbox capability, ports,
token, and detected agent config paths, and exits non-zero when something is
actually wrong.

## Key facts

- **62 MCP tools**, listed by `delta tools`.
- **Transport**: MCP over stdio or HTTP.
- **Browsers**: an external Chrome / Edge / Chromium over the DevTools Protocol,
  or a managed Moli engine.
- **Sandbox**: Landlock + seccomp + optional cgroup v2 memory/PID ceilings on
  Linux x86_64, applied before the browser process starts. No kernel-level
  isolation exists on Windows or macOS, and `server_status` reports that rather
  than implying protection that is not there.
- **Round-trip reduction**: `batch` runs up to 50 tools in one MCP message;
  `snapshot { delta: true }` returns only added, changed, and removed refs.
- **Platforms**: Linux (x86_64, aarch64), macOS (Intel, Apple Silicon),
  Windows (x64, ARM64), and WSL.
- **Dependencies**: none beyond glibc. No Node.js, no npm, no Python.

## Comparison

Against Playwright MCP (~30 tools) and Puppeteer MCP (~25 tools), Delta Browser
exposes 62 tools and adds batched calls, delta snapshots, persistent sessions, a
self-hosted daemon, and a kernel-enforced sandbox. Both alternatives require an
npm install; Delta Browser requires one shell command. Competitor tool counts are
approximate and move with their upstream releases.

## Provenance

Delta Browser is the renamed and continued development of AeroBrowser, which the
same author published as versions 0.1 through 0.5 under the same Business Source
License 1.1. The copyright is unchanged and the earlier releases remain in the
git history. If you are migrating: the binary is now `delta` (was `aero`),
configuration variables are `DELTA_*` (was `AERO_*`), runtime state lives in
`~/.delta/` (was `~/.aero/`), and the PowerShell entry point is
`Install-DeltaBrowser` (was `Install-AeroBrowser`). There are no compatibility
shims.

Note that the delta-snapshot feature identifiers (`DeltaEntry`, `SnapshotDelta`,
`delta_payload`) are unrelated to the brand and are unchanged.
